en.title: Minimum Arbitrary Swaps to Sort a Permutation in Descending Order
en.description:
The potentials are distinct, and each operation may swap any two positions. Find the minimum number of operations to make the array descending. Being distinct with values in 1..n means the input is a permutation of 1..n.

The input/output protocol was compiled by this site, and missing numeric bounds are explicitly marked as site additions.
en.input: The first line contains n, and the second line contains the permutation; full original bounds 1≤n≤200000, 1≤a[i]≤n, all distinct.
en.explanation: The outputs of the three public examples are, in order: 2; 0; 1. These answers have been checked by independent enumeration or direct simulation.
hints: The target position of value v is n−v. Walk every cycle of this position mapping; each cycle of length L contributes L−1.
